# Design Document ## Overview The work splits into three layers that can land one after another: 1. **Model + rendering**: `Style` gains fill rule, opacities and stroke options; `RectShape` gains corner radii; `TextShape` gains an anchor. All defaults equal today's behaviour. Rendering, hit-testing, bounds, booleans, `.p2s` (v4) and SVG writing learn the new fields. 2. **UI**: the style editor and selection panel show the new fields, through generic style operations. 3. **SVG reader**: a CSS module, a reworked cascade, ``/`` expansion, tspan runs, and counted import notes shown in a dialog after opening. No new runtime dependency: the CSS subset is small enough to parse by hand (a full CSS library such as `tinycss2` + `cssselect2` would bring a cascade for selectors we deliberately don't support). ## Steering Document Alignment ### Technical Standards (tech.md) - Frozen dataclasses, changed with `dataclasses.replace`; Qt-free layers below `views/`. - Skia paint setup in one place (`render/paths.py`), matching SVG defaults. - `.p2s` changes follow the migration rule: `CURRENT_VERSION` 3 → 4, migration, sample, `docs/file-format.md` row. - `svgelements` stays limited to parsing path data, colours, lengths and transforms. ### Project Structure (structure.md) - `models/shapes.py`: new fields. - `geometry/segments.py`, `geometry/transforms.py`, `geometry/booleans.py`: rounded rect outline, radii under transforms, fill-rule normalization for booleans. - `render/paths.py`, `render/scene.py`, `render/text.py`, `render/hit_test.py`: paint, opacity, anchor. - `formats/css.py` (new), `formats/svg.py`, `formats/svg_notes.py` (new), `formats/p2s.py`, `formats/p2s_migrations.py`. - `editing/operations/style.py`, `editing/operations/shapes.py` (radius, anchor). - `views/style_editor.py`, `views/selection_view.py`, `views/tool_options_view.py`, `views/import_report_dialog.py` (new), `views/main_window.py`. ## Code Reuse Analysis ### Existing Components to Leverage - **`render/paths.stroke_paint`**: becomes `stroke_paint(style, width=None)`, building cap/join/miter/dash from the style. Used by drawing and `PathCache.stroke_path`, so hit-testing follows dashes and caps automatically. - **`PathCache`**: cached skia paths get their fill type from the shape's style; cache keys are the frozen shapes, so style changes rebuild entries as today. - **`geometry/segments.rect_segments` / `ellipse_segments`**: rounded corners reuse the ellipse kappa constant for the quarter arcs. - **`booleans.combine_parts` / `divide`**: take outlines; evenodd outlines are normalized first (see below), so their internals don't change. - **`svg._Reader`, `_merge_style`, `_parse_transform`, `_length`, `_color`**: extended rather than replaced. - **`editing/operations/style._restyle`**: already generic over `Style` fields; new public operations are thin wrappers. - **`views/unit_fields.LengthSpinBox`**: radius, dash and offset fields in the document unit. - **Import notes**: `read_svg_with_notes` / `read_shapes_svg` already return notes; open and paste already pass them on. ### Integration Points - **Open**: `documents.open_file` stores the notes in `AppState.import_notes`; `MainWindow.open_path` shows the report dialog when that list is non-empty and clears it through an operation. - **Paste**: unchanged path, notes in the status message. - **Recovery / `.p2s`**: shapes go through `encode_style`/`decode_style` and the per-type shape codecs, so recovery snapshots carry the new fields for free. ## Architecture ```mermaid graph TD SVGText[SVG text] --> Reader[svg._Reader] Reader --> CSS[formats/css.py
parse + match] Reader --> Defs[id index
use/symbol expansion] Reader --> Notes[svg_notes.NoteCollector] Reader --> Model[Shapes with full Style] Model --> P2S[p2s v4] Model --> Writer[svg writer] Model --> Render[render/paths + scene
fill type, paints, opacity layer] Model --> Geo[geometry
rounded rect, fill-rule normalize] Geo --> Bool[booleans / Composites] Model --> UI[StyleEditor / SelectionOptions] UI --> Ops[editing/operations/style + shapes] Ops --> Model Notes --> Open[documents.open_file] --> Dialog[ImportReportDialog] ``` ## Components and Interfaces ### 1. Model (`models/shapes.py`) ```python FillRule = Literal["nonzero", "evenodd"] LineCap = Literal["butt", "round", "square"] LineJoin = Literal["miter", "round", "bevel"] TextAnchor = Literal["start", "middle", "end"] @dataclass(frozen=True) class Style: fill: str | None = "#3b82f6" stroke: str | None = "#18181b" stroke_width: float = 2.0 opacity: float = 1.0 # whole object, 0..1 fill_opacity: float = 1.0 stroke_opacity: float = 1.0 fill_rule: FillRule = "nonzero" cap: LineCap = "butt" join: LineJoin = "miter" miter_limit: float = 4.0 dashes: tuple[float, ...] = () # even length, all >= 0, sum > 0; () = solid dash_offset: float = 0.0 RectShape: + rx: float = 0.0, ry: float = 0.0 (appended after `transform`, so existing positional construction stays valid) TextShape: + anchor: TextAnchor = "start" (appended after `transform`) ``` Colours stay `#rrggbb`; alpha always lives in the opacity fields. Opacities are stored 0..1 and shown as percent. `dashes` is normalized to even length on every entry point (import, decoder, operation), so renderers never see an odd list. ### 2. Geometry - **`segments.rect_segments(x, y, w, h, rx=0.0, ry=0.0)`**: clamps radii to w/2, h/2 (SVG rule: if only one is non-zero, `rx = ry`, done by the reader), emits lines + four quarter-arc cubics with `_KAPPA`; zero radii give today's segments exactly. - **`transforms.outline`**: rects pass their radii. - **`transforms.transform_shape(shape, m, min_extent=0.0, scale_radii=False)`**: rects keep `rx`/`ry` by default (handles, numeric fields: Requirement 4.5). The SVG reader passes `scale_radii=True` so a `` under `scale()` keeps its look; in the skew branch the matrix is kept whole, so radii are untouched either way. - **`transforms.area_outline(shape)`**: `outline(shape)` made nonzero-safe: for `fill_rule == "evenodd"` it runs `booleans.simplify(segments, evenodd=True)` (pathops `simplify` with `FillType.EVEN_ODD`, result winding-safe). Used by booleans, divide, Composite part outlines and Composite creation, never by drawing (stroking must follow the original contours). - **`booleans.simplify(segments, evenodd)`**: new small helper next to `combine_parts`. ### 3. Rendering (`render/`) - **`paths.to_skia_path(segments, fill_rule="nonzero")`**: sets `kEvenOdd` or `kWinding`. `_build` passes `shape.style.fill_rule`; text keeps winding. - **`paths.stroke_paint(style, width=None)`**: cap, join, miter limit, and `DashPathEffect` when `style.dashes` (skipped when all lengths are 0). `width` overrides for hit-test widening. Old call sites `stroke_paint(width)` (overlays) become `hairline`/explicit paints; they never used style. - **Bounds**: stroke outset becomes `half * factor` where factor is `max(1, √2 if cap == "square", miter_limit if join == "miter" and the path has corners)`. To stay cheap and identical to today for default styles, the miter term is kept as today (not applied); square caps add √2. Bounds remain a cull/selection approximation as now. - **`scene._paints(style)`**: multiplies `fill_opacity`/`stroke_opacity` (and `opacity`, when only one paint is drawn) into the paint alpha. - **`scene.draw_shape`**: when `opacity < 1` **and** both fill and stroke are painted, wraps the shape in `canvas.saveLayerAlpha(bounds, alpha)` / `restore()`; otherwise no layer (Requirement 2.2, performance requirement). Opacity 0 skips drawing entirely but hit-testing ignores opacity (Requirement 2.9). - **Rounded rects**: `_draw_local` uses `canvas.drawRRect(skia.RRect.MakeRectXY(rect, rx, ry), paint)` when radii are non-zero (GPU fast path), `drawRect` otherwise. - **`text.anchor_offset(shape) -> float`**: `-advance * {start: 0, middle: 0.5, end: 1}` using the same `_font` measurement. `text_blob` drawing and `text_path` both shift x by it, so canvas, export, hit-testing and bounds agree. Rotation stays about `(x, y)`, the anchor point. - **`hit_test._area`**: unchanged logic; fill regions now carry the fill type, so `contains` respects evenodd holes; stroke regions come from the dashed/capped `stroke_path`. ### 4. CSS (`formats/css.py`, new, Qt-free) ```python @dataclass(frozen=True) class Compound: # one simple selector sequence, e.g. path.st0#a tag: str | None # None = any id: str | None classes: frozenset[str] def matches(self, tag: str, element_id: str | None, classes: frozenset[str]) -> bool specificity -> tuple[int, int, int] @dataclass(frozen=True) class Rule: selector: Compound declarations: tuple[tuple[str, str, bool], ...] # property, value, important order: int @dataclass class Stylesheet: rules: list[Rule] skipped: int # rules dropped for unsupported syntax def declarations_for(self, tag, element_id, classes) -> tuple[dict[str, str], dict[str, str]] """(normal, important) declarations, cascaded by specificity then order.""" def parse(text: str, order_start: int = 0) -> Stylesheet ``` - Tokenizing: strip `/* */` comments; skip at-rules (balanced braces for block at-rules like `@media {...}`, up to `;` for `@import`); split `selectors { declarations }`. Comma lists become one `Rule` per selector. A selector containing whitespace combinators, `>`, `+`, `~`, `[`, `:` is unsupported: the rule is dropped and `skipped` counts it (once per rule, not per selector). - Declarations split on `;` outside parentheses and quotes; `!important` stripped and flagged; property names lower-cased. - Indexed by tag/id/class for speed: `declarations_for` looks up candidate rules through dicts (`by_id`, `by_class`, `by_tag`, `universal`), so a few hundred rules don't cost per-element scans (performance requirement). ### 5. SVG reader (`formats/svg.py`) **Cascade.** `_merge_style(inherited, element, sheet)` becomes: 1. start from inherited **inheritable** properties; 2. presentation attributes; 3. stylesheet normal declarations; 4. inline `style` normal declarations; 5. stylesheet `!important` declarations; 6. inline `!important` declarations. `_STYLE_KEYS` grows to: fill, stroke, stroke-width, display, visibility, font-size, fill-opacity, stroke-opacity, fill-rule, stroke-linecap, stroke-linejoin, stroke-miterlimit, stroke-dasharray, stroke-dashoffset, text-anchor. `opacity` is **not** inherited in SVG: it's read per element and passed down as a separate `group_opacity` multiplier in `visit(...)`; a `` with opacity < 1 that holds more than one shape adds the "group opacity approximated" note. `display:none` is not inherited either but hides the subtree (as today); `visibility: hidden` is inherited and skips shapes (with `visible` re-enabling). **Paint.** `_paint(style_text) -> (hex | None, alpha)`: `svgelements.Color` already parses `rgba()`, `hsla()`, `#rgba`, `#rrggbbaa`; alpha multiplies into `fill_opacity`/`stroke_opacity`. `url(...)` keeps the grey fallback and counts a "gradient or pattern" note. **Stroke options.** Parsed with fallbacks to defaults; `stroke-dasharray` accepts commas/spaces and lengths, odd lists repeated, negative values or all-zero → solid; dash lengths and offset scaled by the same √|det| factor as `stroke_width`. **Stylesheets.** Before visiting, the reader collects every `
